newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso ends down on reported cenbank move.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso ends down on reported cenbank move.

text.p: The peso closed 4.7 lower at 1,019.70 on reports the central bank will require banks to keep part of their reserves in dollars, interbank dealers said.

The reports, including one in Tuesday's editions of the Bogota daily El Espectador, said the move was to curb the peso's recent sharp rise against the dollar, which has prompted calls by exporters for a one-off devaluation.
The reports could not be immediately confirmed, but they triggered widespread dollar-buying by banks and other financial institutions, dealers said.
Dealers reported 335 trades in Tuesday's session for a total of $128 million and said the peso hit an intraday high of 1,017.05 before slipping lower ahead of the close.
Minimum dollar positions were required by the central bank until earlier this year, when they were removed because of the peso's fall against the dollar on mounting political uncertainty.
The peso hit a low for the year of 1,074 to the dollar in early June, before making a comeback on rising oil revenues and foreign investment flows.
